events.title: Dead hauler
events.text: A bulk hauler drifts with its running lights still on. Nobody answers. The cargo doors are open, which is either good news or very bad news.

outcomes.text: The crew comes back with a crate of parts and a few things nobody asks about.
A pressure door gives on the way out. Someone will feel it tomorrow, but the crate came too.
Loose change and canned food from the galley. Nobody gets hurt.
Some things are best left drifting.

events.title: Gutted tug
events.text: Someone got here first. The tug's been picked over by people in a hurry, and people in a hurry miss things.

outcomes.text: Under a deck plate: a part, still in its wrapping.
Nothing but cut wiring and a strongly worded note. Some loose change, at least.
Half a pallet of ration packs, only slightly past their date.
Whoever picked it over can have the rest.

events.title: Company wreck
events.text: A Con-Reg survey boat, holed and abandoned. Its transponder is still pinging head office, faithful to the last.

outcomes.text: Good parts, company issue. The transponder logs your visit, naturally.
Pinger out, then the shopping. A clean job.
The pinger was wired to a charge. Company humour. You still get the till.
A breacher's rivet gun, stencilled and signed for. The pinger tells head office who signed for it next.
Not worth the paperwork.

events.title: Halloran drop
events.text: A sealed cargo pod on a slow drift, a Halloran tag on the hatch and no ship in sight. Somebody's drop, waiting for somebody's pickup.

outcomes.text: Machine parts, and cash in a coffee tin. The Hallorans count their drops. They'll know who came by.
The pod was wired, as the family's pods are. Somebody will feel it tomorrow, but the tin came too.
You read the tag out on the family's band. A voice says thank you, which the Hallorans never say. Someone will remember.
Not your drop. Not your problem.

events.title: Cold reactor
events.text: A freighter adrift with her reactor scrammed and stable. A whole core in its cradle is worth a fortune to the right yard, if it stays stable on the way out.

outcomes.text: Your engineer walks the core out of its cradle like a nervous dog. It's yours now.
The core spits as it comes free, and your engineer takes the burn. The core comes anyway.
Blankets, tins and a jar of coins under a bunk. Nobody needs a reactor for that.
Stable is a relative term. You leave it be.

events.title: Seed ark
events.text: An old colony ark, her sleepers long dead in their pods. Her hydroponics bays still glow green, tended by machines that never got the news.

outcomes.text: Lettuce, beans and something like rice, by the crate.
Something in the bays bites. You come away with half a crate and a bandaged hand.
Your xenobiologist sorts the seed stock by hand. Some of it sells, and some of it you eat.
The machines go on gardening for nobody.

events.title: Silent gunboat
events.text: A pirate gunboat, dark and listing, her guns still on their mounts. Pirates don't leave guns behind. Unless they're coming back for them.

outcomes.text: The guns come off clean. Nobody comes back for them.
They were coming back. Her sister ship comes round the far side with her guns hot.
Your scout spots the second ship tucked in her shadow. You take what you can reach and go quietly.
Her gunner's autogun, racked and oiled, a drum still on it. Nobody comes back for it.
They were coming back. Her sister ship comes round the far side with her guns hot.
Some bait is too obvious to take.

events.title: Holed tanker
events.text: A water tanker split along her spine, her cargo spilling out in a slow, glittering cloud of ice.

outcomes.text: Water is food, out here. The holds take what they can.
Your engineer pulls a water reclaimer out whole. Somebody will want it.
The cloud glitters on behind you.

events.title: Dead mail runner
events.text: A courier drone out of fuel, her hold full of letters nobody will ever read. The postmark is three years old.

outcomes.text: Bank codes, mostly expired. Not all of them. Someone will notice.
Love letters and complaints, and a little cash folded into a birthday card.
Your pilot plots the drop. The lanes pay a postage bounty, and honest ships draw fewer eyes.
Three more years won't hurt it.

events.title: Wayside shrine
events.text: A shrine built into a dead hull by passing spacers: candles in jars, ration tins, photographs, a wrench polished bright.

outcomes.text: Coins, mostly, and a good wrench. Nobody's watching. Probably.
Coins and a good wrench. Then a run of bad luck: the airlock bites everyone on the way out.
Old hands know the custom: take what you need, leave what you can. You need rations.
You leave it as you found it. Someone in the crew lights a candle.

events.title: Stray nav buoy
events.text: A lane buoy knocked off its station, blinking the wrong numbers at nobody.

outcomes.text: Your pilot nudges it home. The lanes pay a finder's fee and log you as helpful.
Its power cells sell well. The buoy screams on every band as it dies.
Somebody else can get lost by it.

events.title: Gutted cutter
events.text: A pirate cutter holed and dead. Her spares locker is still sealed, which is more than anyone can say for her crew.

outcomes.text: Spares, the right sizes. The worst of your wrecks is working again before you cast off.
One gun, unbolted and stowed.
The gun was wired to go off. It did. You keep the gun.
Under a dead man's laundry, a sawn-off and a box of shells.
Her crew can keep her.

events.title: Stalled miner
events.text: A mining skiff on the emergency band: drive dead, two aboard, rations low, union pins on their collars. They can pay, they say. Miners always say that.

outcomes.text: They pay, and in cash. Somewhere a pig is flying.
They pay in IOUs and a bag of ore samples. Worth about what you'd think.
They swear they never saw you. Word gets around the right way.
The band goes quiet behind you.

events.title: Odd beacon
events.text: A distress beacon on a band nobody uses any more. It could be someone in trouble. It could be someone making trouble.

outcomes.text: A lone prospector, grateful and flush. She tips well and shares her rations.
Claim jumpers. You get away, but not clean, and they'll talk.
Not your problem. Probably.

events.title: Lost courier
events.text: A courier pod with a cracked nav core, asking for a fix and a heading. The sender paid for delivery, and you look like delivery.

outcomes.text: Twenty minutes with a wrench and a heading. The fee clears. The pod's log mentions you.
Inside: bearer bonds. Someone will miss those.
Inside: somebody's mail. Now the pod is screaming about it.
It'll find its own way. Or it won't.

events.title: Fleet tender
events.text: A Fleet supply tender on the emergency band, reactor scrammed, a midshipman reading regulations into the mic. The Fleet doesn't ask civilians for help. This one is asking.

outcomes.text: The reactor's back on your spares, and the midshipman logs you a friend of the Fleet. Pirates took her other stores pod: the Fleet would like it home.
Their stores pod is right there, and they can't move to stop you. The midshipman takes your registration down, very slowly.
The midshipman is still reading regulations as the band fades.

events.title: Survey skiff
events.text: A Con-Reg survey skiff with a cracked drive housing, two surveyors in company orange asking for a tow to the lanes. They're very polite. They haven't checked your registration yet.

outcomes.text: They sign for the tow on a company form, in triplicate. A good word goes up the line, for what that's worth at Con-Reg.
Survey cores sell well to the right broker, and you know three. The surveyors will file a complaint. Con-Reg reads every one.
The skiff's lights shrink behind you, blinking politely.

events.title: Fever ship
events.text: A family hauler flying the yellow flag: fever aboard, no medic, a child coughing on the open band. They can pay, a little.

outcomes.text: Your medic doses the lot of them. They pay what they can, and the kids wave from the viewport.
They pay, and your medic brings the fever home. A day in the bunk, maybe two.
A crate from the medical stores, sent across on a line. They swear they never saw you.
The coughing follows you a while on the band.

events.title: Lifeboat beacon
events.text: A lifeboat's beacon on the emergency band, strong and steady. Lifeboats don't usually drift this straight.

outcomes.text: Two miners, half frozen and very grateful. They tip in ore money and share their rations.
The lifeboat is empty and the beacon is bait. A cutter drops out of the dark behind you.
Your scout reads the drift: nobody drifts that straight. You leave the bait for someone else.
The beacon keeps calling. Not to you.

events.title: Jammed airlock
events.text: A survey crew locked inside their own ship by a jammed airlock, reading out their air on the band in a careful voice.

outcomes.text: Your engineer has the lock open in ten minutes. They pay in cash, and in tears.
The hatch goes, and so does some of their paint. They pay anyway.
The hatch goes harder than planned. Someone on your side takes a piece of it.
They're still reading out their air as the band fades.

events.title: Runaway tug
events.text: An automated ore tug, its brain fried, pushing a rock the size of a station toward the lanes.

outcomes.text: Your pilot gets alongside and talks it into a safe orbit. The lanes are grateful, and don't ask your name.
A part off its hull, grabbed on the fly.
The rock clips you on the way out. Something aboard takes it badly.
Someone else can stop it. Someone will. Probably.

events.title: Mutiny on the band
events.text: A freighter's captain on the band, locked in her cabin, her crew holding the bridge. She'll pay for help, she says, if she lives.

outcomes.text: Your marine settles it in three minutes. The captain pays, and keeps paying.
Settled, after a fashion. Your marine wears the bruises; the captain pays.
You never raise your voice. By the end of it they're apologising to her. She pays you anyway.
Not your ship. Not your mutiny.

events.title: Burning barge
events.text: A barge with a fire in her hold, venting smoke, her crew asking anyone at all for help with it.

outcomes.text: Your engineer smothers it from outside. Her captain pays in cash, gratefully.
Smothered, and your engineer takes a scorching for it. The captain pays.
Her crew are busy with the fire. Her cargo isn't. They watch you take it.
The smoke trails behind you for an hour.

events.title: Red flare
events.text: A red flare off the lane: the old sign for a ship in trouble. Also the old sign for an ambush.

outcomes.text: A courier with a busted drive, paying in spares for a tow.
An ambush, as old as the flare. A cutter comes round the rock with her guns out.
Your marine on the guns. Whoever set the flare thinks better of it, and leaves their flare gun behind.
The flare burns out behind you.

events.title: Ration barge
events.text: A family barge selling food out of the hold. The prices are fair. The cat is not for sale.

outcomes.text: Six crates of the good stuff. Well, the edible stuff.
Twelve crates, and a jar of pickles thrown in.
The cat watches you go.

events.title: Scrap dealer
events.text: A dealer with a hold full of junk and an eye for yours. He buys parts, no questions asked, and sells rations to anyone with cash.

outcomes.text: He looks it over, sniffs, and pays. Fair enough.
Six crates. He counts the change twice.
A machine pistol from the bottom of a crate of junk. It fires. He shows you.
He's already looking at the next ship.

events.title: Co-op barge
events.text: A barge in union colours, selling rations at cost to members and with a markup to everyone else. The purser would like to know which you are.

outcomes.text: Six crates, at the markup. The purser is polite about it.
The purser writes you a receipt, and the radio does the rest. The halls will hear you paid in.
The purser waves you off, union fashion.

events.title: Tinker's barge
events.text: A tinker with a hold full of tools and a sign hand-painted on the hull: REPAIRS. CASH. NO QUESTIONS.

outcomes.text: Cash, no questions. She has the worst of it working in an afternoon.
Two jobs, one price, and she hums the whole time.
She's already painting the next sign.

events.title: Bulk rations
events.text: A grain hauler selling off a spoiled shipment cheap. Mostly spoiled, the captain says. He won't say how mostly.

outcomes.text: Mostly is about half. Twelve crates of the good stuff.
Mostly is more than half. Six crates you'd eat.
Your quartermaster knows good grain by the smell. Twelve crates, every one sound.
He's still shouting prices as you leave.

events.title: Fence
events.text: A fence with a ship full of other people's things, buying anything that isn't nailed down and some things that are.

outcomes.text: He pays fair, for a fence. His buyers talk, though.
He knows who's looking for you, and where they aren't.
He pays you to go away. It's a business expense.
His bodyguard leans back. You leave with some of his money and a cut lip.
He's already pricing your ship.

events.title: Ship's chandler
events.text: A chandler's barge: spares, stores, rope and gossip, all sold by the kilo.

outcomes.text: The right spares, at the wrong price. The worst of your wrecks is working again.
You learn where the hunters were seen last, and where they weren't.
You learn some things. The chandler learns more. Your name, for one.
Tins, flour and coffee by the kilo, swung across in a net.
The chandler waves with a rope in each hand.

events.title: Arms dealer
events.text: A quiet ship selling quiet guns. The dealer's prices aren't quiet at all.

outcomes.text: A gun, crated, with the serials filed off.
Your marine knows guns, and tells him so at length. He knocks a third off to make it stop.
A Con-Reg rail rifle, serials and all. He won't say how he came by it, and charges for not saying.
He doesn't wave. Dealers don't.

events.title: Data broker
events.text: A data broker selling charts, codes and rumour from a ship that's mostly antennas.

outcomes.text: Charts with the patrol routes marked. Old, but not that old.
Your logs say where you've been. Now so does everyone she sells them to.
Her antennas swivel to follow you out.

events.title: Junk auction
events.text: A salvage barge auctioning sealed crates, sight unseen, to whoever's in range of her band.

outcomes.text: A part in the crate, still in its foam.
Ration bars. A lot of ration bars.
Your scout watches who bids on what, and you bid on the crate the dealer's cousin wanted.
The auctioneer is still talking when the band cuts out.

events.title: Ion storm
events.text: The instruments go white. An ion storm is rolling through, and the ship is in the middle of it.

outcomes.text: Lights flicker, coffee spills, nothing breaks.
A panel blows in the corridor. Everyone has a scorch mark to show for it.
Burning hard eats into the stores, but nobody gets cooked.

events.title: Loose rock
events.text: A field of drifting rock, thick enough to scrape paint. Thick enough to scrape worse.

outcomes.text: Not a scratch. The pilot will be insufferable.
A rock comes through the forward plating. Someone takes it on the shoulder.
Slow and dull, and nobody gets hurt.
The rocks hide you from anyone watching.
The rocks hide you, and one of them hits you.

events.title: Micrometeor sleet
events.text: Sand-sized rock at orbital speed, hissing off the hull like rain on a tin roof. Most of it bounces.

outcomes.text: Hiss, rattle, and silence. Nothing important was hit.
Something important was hit. The board lights up red.
Burning hard eats into the stores, but the hull stays whole.
Your pilot tucks the ship in behind a rock until it passes. Not a scratch.

events.title: Solar flare
events.text: The local star throws a flare. Every screen aboard goes white, then dark, then white again.

outcomes.text: The screens come back. Everything still works. Everyone checks twice.
The screens come back, and one system doesn't.
A day cold and dark, eating out of tins. The flare passes, nothing breaks, and nobody saw you in the glare.
Your engineer pulls the right breakers in the right order. Nothing fries.

events.title: Gravity well
events.text: A dead star, dense and dark, missing from the charts. The ship's course is already bending toward it.

outcomes.text: Your pilot throws you round it and out the far side, faster and harder to follow.
Every thruster you have, for an hour, and the stores to show for it.
A long, slow, sickening curve. Nobody throws up. Nearly nobody.
The curve tightens. Everyone aboard spends it pinned to the deck.

events.title: Static cloud
events.text: A cloud of charged dust that crawls over the hull in sparks. It's very pretty. It's eating the paint.

outcomes.text: Your engineer grounds the hull, and the sparks run off into the dark.
The sparks die behind you, and the cloud hides you as well as anything could.
The cloud hides you, and shorts something out on the way.
The long way round. The paint survives.

events.title: Ice field
events.text: A field of dirty ice, tumbling slow, thick enough to hide in and full of water.

outcomes.text: Ice, melted down for the stores.
Ice, and a block of it on someone's arm.
A day nosing through the ice, eating and waiting. Anyone watching loses you.
Nothing mined, and nobody hurt.

events.title: Old minefield
events.text: A minefield from a war nobody won. Most of the mines are dead. Most.

outcomes.text: Your scout marks the live ones. The dead ones are full of parts.
Nothing goes off. Everyone breathes out at once, and nobody follows you through.
One goes off. Not close, but close enough. Nobody follows you through.
A long day round the edge of it, and the stores to show for it.

events.title: Radiation belt
events.text: A belt of hard radiation round a dead gas giant. The shortcut runs right through it.

outcomes.text: Everyone glows a little. Nobody follows you through.
Your medic doses everyone before the run. Nobody glows, and nobody follows.
The long way round, and the safe one.

events.title: Drive shudder
events.text: The drive starts to shudder. Something in the coupling is working loose, and the noise is getting worse.

outcomes.text: Your engineer finds the loose coupling, and fixes the old wreck next to it while in there.
It shakes, and rattles, and holds.
It doesn't hold. Something gives with a bang.

events.title: Comet's tail
events.text: A comet's tail, thick with ice and gas, glittering across a thousand kilometres of dark.

outcomes.text: Ice by the hold-load, scooped as you pass.
Ice by the hold-load, and a rock inside the ice.
Your pilot skims it slow and steady. Ice, and no rocks.
It glitters on behind you.

events.title: Company courier
events.text: A Con-Reg courier on the emergency band, begging a tow. Her registration says courier. Her hull plates say otherwise.

outcomes.text: She's real, and the Company pays its tows, eventually. A credit note, at least.
Her hull plates were right. The courier drops her disguise: a repo tug, grapples out.
Your engineer reads the plates: repo tug, painted over. You leave her calling.
The Company can tow its own.

events.title: Union runner
events.text: A union boat running parts to striking halls, selling a few on the side to anyone who isn't the Company.

outcomes.text: Salvage, union-priced. The purser writes you a receipt anyway.
The purser puts it in the strike fund, and tells you where the repo crews drink.
The purser waves you off, union fashion.

events.title: Old shift crew
events.text: Miners from your old shift on the Tailings, broke and stranded and very glad to hear your voice. They still owe the Company too.

outcomes.text: Four days of rations and a lot of old stories. The halls will hear you looked after your own.
They'll pay it back, they say. They tell you where the repo crews are working instead.
Their voices fade into the static, still telling stories.

events.title: Debt ledger
events.text: A Con-Reg records skiff, gutted, its ledger core still humming. Your debt is in there somewhere, with everyone else's.

outcomes.text: Your engineer wipes it clean. A lot of debts just got harder to collect, yours among them.
A broker pays well for Company ledgers. The Company pays better to learn who sold one.
Let it hum.

events.title: Amnesty beacon
events.text: A Fleet beacon broadcasting an amnesty for deserters: come home, it says, and all is forgiven. The Provost wrote it.

outcomes.text: It's real, more or less. A clerk logs you as returning and forgets to finish the form.
Nothing is forgiven. A Provost cutter comes out of the beacon's shadow.
Your pilot still knows the Fleet's beacon codes. It goes on broadcasting to nobody.
Forgiveness can wait.

events.title: Old division
events.text: A hired barge full of Fleet sailors on shore leave: your old division. They know your face.

outcomes.text: They drink to you, and swear they never saw you.
Your old mates fix what they can, for old times' sake.
Someone in the division talks to the Provost before you're out of range.
They sing you out on the band. Badly.

events.title: Fleet cache
events.text: A Fleet supply cache in a dead hull, sealed with codes you used to know by heart.

outcomes.text: Your marine still knows the codes. Rations and cash, signed for by nobody.
Rations and cash, and an alarm screaming on the Fleet band.
The cache defends itself. Someone takes a shock, and the alarm screams on.
The Fleet can keep its cache.

events.title: Deserters' den
events.text: A ship full of deserters like you, trading forged papers and old grudges.

outcomes.text: New names, new numbers, and a Provost file that ends in a dead end.
They pay well for Fleet codes. The Fleet will know whose.
They wave. Nobody uses names.

events.title: Warm drop
events.text: A Halloran cargo pod drifting where no pod should be, its tag still warm.

outcomes.text: A real drop, careless of them. Parts, and a tin of cash.
The pod was a lure. A Halloran runner was waiting in the dust.
Your quartermaster knows the family's tags: this one's a lure. You leave it be.
Not your drop. Not this time.

events.title: Old fence
events.text: Your old fence from the Narrows, running a quiet barge out past the lanes. She's glad to see you. She's always glad to see money.

outcomes.text: She pays over the odds, for old times' sake.
She knows where the Hallorans are looking, and where they've given up.
She blows you a kiss on the band.

events.title: Customs cutter
events.text: A customs cutter on the emergency band: drive out, crew of two, hold full of seized cargo. Seized from people like you.

outcomes.text: You tow the customs men home. The Fleet logs you as helpful, which is a first.
Seized cargo, seized again. Customs takes your registration, very slowly.
Customs can tow customs.

events.title: Your old cache
events.text: A cache you hid years ago in a dead freighter, before the Hallorans burned you. Still there, if nobody found it.

outcomes.text: Cash and rations, right where you left them.
Cash and rations, and someone was watching your old cache.
Your scout checks the dark first. Nobody's watching. Cash and rations.
Some savings are better left saved.

events.title: Cold hauler
events.text: A hauler with her lights out and her holds still sealed. Whoever left her left in a hurry, and took nothing with them.

outcomes.text: The squad cracks the holds and brings back a crate of parts and some of her plating.
A hold door gives on the way out. Someone takes the weight of it, but the crate came too.
Hull plates, cut and stacked in the hold. Slow work, and nobody gets hurt.
Some ships are better left as they are.

events.title: Picked-over liner
events.text: A passenger liner, stripped long ago by someone in a hurry. They never got as far as the engine room.

outcomes.text: Behind a jammed hatch: a part still in its mounts, and nobody else's name on it.
The hatch was jammed for a reason. The squad gets out with some scrap and a burn or two.
Sealed rations by the case, still good, or good enough.
The squad looks once round her dark decks and turns for home.

events.title: Squatters' camp
events.text: A hauler with fresh scorch marks on her hull and a light on in her galley. Somebody lives aboard.

outcomes.text: They left in a hurry, and left their stores.
They didn't leave. The squatters come out of the holds, armed.
You never raise your voice. They trade food for news, and point you at the next wreck.
Live and let live.

events.title: Ghost freighter
events.text: A freighter with her lights out and her airlock open, and a fresh boot print in the frost on her deck.

outcomes.text: Whoever left the print is long gone. Their crate isn't.
Whoever left the print was waiting in the dark.
Your scout reads the frost: one set of prints, going out. The squad strips her in peace.
The print stays in the frost.

events.title: Intact engine room
events.text: A tug with her bow torn away and her engine room still pressurised, its spares racked neatly.

outcomes.text: Spares for the ship's worst wreck, and some plating besides.
Plating, cut and stacked. Slow work.
A cutting torch from her damage-control locker, its tank half full. It cuts plate. It cuts other things.
Her engine room keeps its spares.

events.title: Hospital hulk
events.text: A hospital ship, abandoned in good order, her stores still sealed and her theatre lights still on.

outcomes.text: Your medic unbolts a whole med bay and knows which crates to bring.
Sealed rations by the case.
The theatre lights stay on behind you.

events.title: Dead gunboat
events.text: A gunboat with her guns still mounted and her crew long gone.

outcomes.text: Your engineer unbolts a turret whole. The colony could use it.
Armour plate by the slab.
Armour plate by the slab, and a slab on someone's foot.
Most of her racks are bare. The last holds a riot gun, still in its grease.
A riot gun in its grease, and a rack that comes down on someone's arm.
Her guns stay aimed at nobody.

events.title: Sleeper ship
events.text: A colony ship with her sleepers still in their pods, long past waking. Her seed vault reads cold and sealed.

outcomes.text: Your xenobiologist sorts the good seed from the dead: a season's planting, and something to eat now.
Plating and beams. Nobody looks at the pods.
You leave the sleepers sleeping.

events.title: Leaking tanker
events.text: A fuel tanker venting a slow, glittering leak. Her hull plating is the light, good kind.

outcomes.text: Light plating, stacked in the hold.
A spark in the wrong place. Everyone comes home singed.
Careful, every cut of it. Light plating, and no sparks.
Leaks are someone else's problem.

events.title: Old battle
events.text: Wreckage from a fight nobody won, spread thin across a thousand kilometers of nothing.

outcomes.text: Plating, beams and cable: a hold's worth, slowly.
A tumbling beam catches someone on the way back in, but the hold is full.
One part came through the fight in one piece, and it comes home.
Everything worth having burned or broke. Nothing comes home.
The dead can keep their field.

events.title: Split cargo pod
events.text: A cargo pod torn open in the field, its crates spinning slowly out of it.

outcomes.text: Food, most of it, and none of it spoiled in the cold.
A crate comes in faster than anyone liked. The food is fine; the one who caught it isn't.
The pod's frame, in pieces, in the hold.
The crates spin on.

events.title: Tagged debris
events.text: A slow cloud of wreckage, every piece tagged and numbered by someone who meant to come back for it.

outcomes.text: Tagged plating, in order. Very convenient.
Your scout reads the tags: the best piece is a whole part.
Someone may yet come back for it.

events.title: Empty escape pods
events.text: A string of escape pods, every one launched and every one empty. Whoever was in them got somewhere.

outcomes.text: Emergency rations and light frames, from every pod.
They got somewhere. Good luck to them.

events.title: Broken ring
events.text: What's left of a mining station, its ring broken in three and slowly turning.

outcomes.text: Ring sections, cut and stacked.
A section turns into someone. Half a hold, and a wound.
In a sealed locker: a part, still in its mounts.
Mostly empty. Some rations.
It turns on without you.

events.title: Drifting tool locker
events.text: A tool locker the size of a cabin, drifting free of whatever it was bolted to.

outcomes.text: Tools and spares: the ship's worst wreck gets seen to on the way home.
Your engineer knows what fits what. Two wrecks seen to before you're home.
It drifts on, full of tools.

events.title: Frozen crates
events.text: Crates of food spilled from a broken hauler, frozen hard and perfectly kept.

outcomes.text: Food, frozen and fine.
Food, frozen and fine, and a crate on someone's hand.
Your quartermaster knows a good crate from a burst one. A full hold.
They'll keep.

events.title: Drone net
events.text: A broken net of old sensor drones, some still blinking at each other across the dark.

outcomes.text: Drone frames, light and strong.
Your engineer gets one working, and it's worth more working.
They blink on.

events.title: Warship's spine
events.text: A warship's spine, kilometres long, picked clean except where it was too heavy to move.

outcomes.text: A section of spine, the best steel for light years.
The section shifts as it comes free. Someone takes the weight of it.
Steady hands find the seams the yard welded. It comes apart like it was made to.
Her bones stay where they fell.

events.title: Rich seam
events.text: A seam of ore shows bright on the rock's sunlit face, wider than the scans said.

outcomes.text: The seam holds all the way down. The ship comes home heavy.
The face slumps halfway down. The squad gets out with half the ore and some bruises.
What comes away easily, and nobody under it.
The ore will keep.

events.title: Ice and iron
events.text: Dirty ice over a core of iron. The squad can cut one or the other before the ship has to turn for home.

outcomes.text: Iron, in slabs, in the hold.
Ice, melted down for the stores: water to drink and to cook with.
The rock tumbles on.

events.title: Crystal pocket
events.text: A hollow in the rock lined with crystals that ring when the squad's lamps touch them.

outcomes.text: Crystal by the crate. It rings all the way home.
One shatters as it comes free. Someone bleeds.
You'd wait all day for the right cut. Today you did. Not one breaks.
It rings softly as the squad goes.

events.title: Old workings
events.text: Shafts sunk by someone long gone, their props still holding. Mostly.

outcomes.text: The old faces still give.
A prop gives. The squad gets out with half a load and bruises.
Your engineer shores the props before anyone goes in. Every face gives.
Someone else can trust the props.

events.title: Ice cave
events.text: A cave of blue ice under the rock's skin, clean enough to drink as it is.

outcomes.text: Ice by the block: water for the stores.
Ice and ore, both.
Ice and ore, and the cave roof drops a slab.
It stays blue and clean.

events.title: Gas pocket
events.text: The scanner says there's a pocket of gas behind the next face. The scanner has been wrong before.

outcomes.text: The scanner was wrong. The face comes down clean.
The scanner was right. Everyone comes out coughing, with half a load.
Twelve-hour shifts on the ore line taught you to vent first. A full load, and nobody coughing.
Some faces are better left.

events.title: Old claim
events.text: A claim marker on the rock, its owner's name worn off, and a cache of tools beneath it.

outcomes.text: Good tools: the ship's worst wreck gets fixed on the way home.
Somebody's claim. Still.

events.title: Metal vein
events.text: A vein of native metal, bright and soft, running deep into the rock.

outcomes.text: The vein holds all the way down.
The face slumps halfway down. Half a load, and bruises.
Built like a cargo lifter, and today it shows. The whole vein comes out.
It'll keep.

events.title: Tumbling rock
events.text: A rock tumbling end over end, too fast to land on and just slow enough to grapple.

outcomes.text: Your pilot matches the tumble. The squad cuts a full load before letting go.
Loose rock, picked out of the spin.
It tumbles on.

events.title: Something grows
events.text: Something green grows in the valleys down there, and the scanners say it won't kill anyone.

outcomes.text: Roots, fruit and something like grain. The hold comes home full.
Something down there bites. The squad comes home with half a hold and a wound.
The squad watches it all the way home.

events.title: Crashed probe
events.text: An old survey probe, crashed into a hillside and half buried. Whoever sent it never came back for it.

outcomes.text: Most of the probe comes out whole, and part of it is worth fitting.
The hillside comes down on the dig. Someone is hurt, but its panels are in the hold.
The probe's panels and frame, light and easy to carry.
It can lie there a while longer.

events.title: Fungus forest
events.text: Towers of fungus taller than the ship, pale and soft. The scanners can't say if they're safe to eat.

outcomes.text: Safe enough. Better than safe: it tastes of bread.
Not safe. Everyone comes home green, with half a load.
Your xenobiologist finds the safe kind. A full hold, and nobody green.
The towers sway in a wind nobody can hear.

events.title: Gone-wild farm
events.text: Fields gone wild around a farmhouse dome, the crops run to seed and still growing.

outcomes.text: Grain gone wild, still good.
Dome panels, light and clear.
It grows on without anyone.

events.title: Grazing herds
events.text: Herds of something big and slow grazing the plains. They don't look dangerous. They don't look small, either.

outcomes.text: Your marine brings one down cleanly. Meat for weeks.
One brought down, and meat for weeks.
It wasn't as slow as it looked. Someone gets trampled; some meat comes home.
They graze on, unconcerned.

events.title: Lander in a ravine
events.text: A colony lander on its side at the bottom of a ravine, its cargo still strapped down.

outcomes.text: A part, still strapped down, hauled up on lines.
The lines slip. Someone falls the last bit, and only some panels come up.
First one down and first one up. The part, and some panels too.
It stays in its ravine.

events.title: Hot springs
events.text: Steaming pools in a high valley, rich in minerals and pleasantly warm.

outcomes.text: Mineral crust, cut in slabs.
Clean water, and plenty of it.
Somebody wanted a bath. Nobody got one.

events.title: Old ruins
events.text: Ruins older than any colony, half buried in red sand. Nobody who built them has ever been asked about it.

outcomes.text: Something useful under the sand, left by somebody useful.
Sand, mostly, and some stone worth cutting.
Your xenobiologist reads where the builders kept their tools. They're still there.
They've waited this long.

events.title: Storm plain
events.text: A plain swept by lightning, glassy with fused sand, a wrecked weather station in the middle of it.

outcomes.text: Panels and wiring, pulled between strikes.
A strike lands close. Someone's hair stands up and stays up.
You flinch at every flash, which is why you're still breathing. Panels, and no burns.
The lightning keeps it.

events.title: Con-Reg courier
events.text: A Con-Reg courier skiff on the emergency band, one engine out. Her hold is full of paper filed again from Depot 4's backups, and yours is in there somewhere.

outcomes.text: Her pilot opens the hold for a tow and doesn't watch what goes out the airlock. Con-Reg's paper on you is a cloud of confetti.
Her pilot did watch. The argument costs someone a bruise, and the paper goes out the airlock all the same.
Someone else will tow her. Your paper will get where it's going.

events.title: The Resolute
events.text: A Fleet tender at anchor, running lights low: the Resolute, your old ship. Her chief is on the open band, asking anyone for spares. The crate you walked off with would have seen her right.

outcomes.text: The chief knows your voice and doesn't say so. He logs the money as a gift from a friend of the Fleet, which the Provost will have to read.
Someone else will see her right. Probably.

events.title: Lost cargo
events.text: Twenty-nine crates still roped together, tumbling slow where you cut them loose, the Hallorans' seal on every one.

outcomes.text: Twenty-nine crates, left at the family's next drop with your compliments. Old Halloran is almost pleased.
They've waited this long.

events.title: Stolen stores pod
events.text: The Fleet tender's other stores pod, tumbling where the pirates left it: seals cut, her number still stencilled on the side. They took the good stuff and left the rest.

outcomes.text: You tow it to the beacon and log it on the Fleet's band. A lieutenant thanks you by name, and a finder's fee follows.
You log the pod on the Fleet's band. The tender's bosun, Ines Varga, asks to come aboard, and the lieutenant signs her over in place of a fee.
Tinned rations and a crate of filters, the tender's number on every tin. The Fleet will know.
It isn't going anywhere.

events.title: Hall food run
events.text: A union barge riding low with rations for a striking hall, her pilot down with fever. The steward at her helm, Teo Brandt, has flown her this far on a docker's licence and a prayer.

outcomes.text: You fly her in on your pilot's hours. Teo stays aboard: the local can find another steward, he says, and you can't find another quartermaster.
The hall eats tonight. Teo shakes every hand aboard, and the local pays what it can for the fuel.
A hold of union rations, and nobody to stop you but a docker at a helm. The halls will hear of it before you're out of the sector.
Teo waves you on, and goes back to reading the barge's manual.

events.title: Company lifepod
events.text: A Con-Reg lifepod on the company band, one aboard: the junior surveyor from the skiff you towed, let go for the fuel the tow cost and put out at the lanes with a lifepod and a reference.

outcomes.text: Ama Osei comes aboard with her survey kit and the Company's reference, which says she is honest to a fault. You'll see.
You see her to a lanes station with a week's rations. She pays you in Company survey lines, which she shouldn't have and you can sell.
Recovery pays a finder's fee on Company property, lifepods included. She doesn't say anything as they take her off.
The pod's beacon blinks on the company band behind you.

events.title: Halloran runner
events.text: A Halloran runner on one engine, her crew patched up in the hold by the family's medic. Dez Halloran heard you call the drop in. The family wants him home, and he would rather not go.

outcomes.text: You tow her to the family's drop, and Dez stays aboard. Old Halloran sends word that the family will want him back.
You tow her to the family's drop. Old Halloran sends his thanks, which he never does.
Her hold is family business, and now it's yours. Dez watches you do it and says nothing, which the family will hear about.
Dez watches you go from her viewport.

events.title: Dust front
events.text: A wall of dust on the horizon, moving fast. The farms are open to the sky.

outcomes.text: Plating over the rows, weighted with rock. The dust goes by and the crops come through.
The dust buries the solar arrays and a shed with them. A week digging out, and what's bent stays bent.
It veers north at the last. Not a leaf touched.

events.title: Fever
events.text: Someone wakes burning up, and by noon a second has it. Nobody knows what it is yet.

outcomes.text: The medic walls off a corner and keeps it there. Three days of soup and it passes.
Water boiled, bedding scalded, rations opened only in the clean room. Slow and wasteful, and nobody else gets it.
It goes through everyone. A bad week, and nobody dies.
It burns out in the two it took. Lucky.

events.title: Ice strike
events.text: The mine's drill comes up wet. A pocket of old ice under the dig, clean enough to drink.

outcomes.text: Tanks full of water and a crop of greens from it within the week.
The heater lines burst on the second day. Water, and a scalded arm.
The ice can wait. The ore next to it can't.

events.title: Survey cache
events.text: An old survey team's marker, half buried, with a cache under it. The seal says forty years.

outcomes.text: Spares, wrapped in oilcloth and still good.
The pit caves in on whoever's at the bottom. The cache comes up anyway.
The marker says where they dug. The scout digs where they didn't.
A flag on the map, and on the list of things to get to.

events.title: Falling scrap
events.text: Something burns up overhead and scatters across the plain. Some of it is still glowing when it lands.

outcomes.text: Plating and wire, still warm, stacked behind the storehouse.
Plating and wire, and a burn from a piece that was hotter than it looked.
By the time it's cool, the wind has scattered most of it. Some is left.

events.title: Grain borers
events.text: Something small is eating through the stores. The sacks are full of holes and the holes are full of grubs.

outcomes.text: It costs a week's food, and the borers go with it.
The xenobiologist turns one over and laughs: they're edible, and better roasted than the rations.
Hours of picking. The store is saved, grub by grub.
Hours of picking, and the grubs bite. The bites swell for days.

events.title: Prowler
events.text: Tracks around the perimeter at dawn, and the fence wire cut in one place. Whatever it was, it walked on two legs.

outcomes.text: A camp in the rocks, empty, and a sidearm left behind in a hurry.
Whoever it was is waiting in the rocks. A shot, a scramble, and they're gone.
Nobody comes back. In the morning there's a crate of scrap by the cut wire, left as an apology.
Locks and a lamp on the fence. The tracks don't come back.

events.title: Tremor
events.text: The ground rolls under the colony for a long ten seconds. The walls are standing. For now.

outcomes.text: Braces on every wall that creaked. Expensive, and nothing falls.
The engineer finds the two walls that matter and braces only those.
A storehouse wall comes down in the night. The materials behind it go with it.
Nothing comes down. Nothing creaked as much as it sounded.

events.title: Lost drone
events.text: A survey drone pings the colony's band, low on charge and circling. Nobody here owns it.

outcomes.text: Wire, cells and a good motor, sorted into the stores.
The pilot talks it down on the last of its charge, whole. Its cargo bay was full.
It comes down hard on the pad. What's left goes in the scrap.
It circles twice more and drifts off east.

events.title: Prospector
events.text: A prospector's crawler grinds in from the hills, one old woman aboard, wanting food and a trade.

outcomes.text: She takes the rations and leaves a crate of spares she won't need.
An old hand knows the stories she wants. She leaves the ore she was carrying.
She grumbles and grinds on west.

events.title: Claim beacon
events.text: A Con-Reg beacon drops from orbit and starts broadcasting: this ore is the Company's, and so are you.

outcomes.text: It makes good wire, the Company's beacon.
It was rigged to burn if opened. It burns.
A tithe goes up on the beacon's lift. The broadcast stops, for now.

events.title: The old shift
events.text: A message on the long band from the crew you used to haul with. They heard you got out. They want to know how.

outcomes.text: They pool what they can spare and send it out on a supply run.
They wish you well. That's all they can spare.
A load of ore for their quota. They won't forget it, and you're short of it.

events.title: Wanted flyer
events.text: A Provost courier drone drops a flyer on the pad: your face, your name, and the Resolute's crate number.

outcomes.text: A courier drone is good wire and better cells.
It was rigged to burn on opening, Provost-style.
It sits there for a week, blinking, and then its battery dies.

events.title: Resolute's crate
events.text: A drop canister lands near the farms, Fleet issue, stencilled RESOLUTE. Someone aboard her still remembers you.

outcomes.text: A rifle and a note: 'You left this.' No name.
Fleet canisters seal hard. It opens on someone's hand.
It goes in the store, sealed, in case.

events.title: Family parcel
events.text: A parcel on the supply drop, wrapped in Halloran green, with a card: 'Thinking of you.'

outcomes.text: Good spares, and the family's compliments.
It goes off in the hands that opened it. A warning, not a killing.
It burns with a bang at the back of the pit. The family will hear you got it.

events.title: Old contact
events.text: A voice on the band you haven't heard since the run that burned you: they're passing, and they have goods.

outcomes.text: Rations for a machine pistol, no questions on either side.
'Suit yourself,' and the band goes quiet.

events.title: Varga's count
events.text: Varga hasn't slept. She has the tender's ration count written on the galley wall, every crate, and who had them last.

outcomes.text: An hour of numbers. At the end of it she knows where the pirates went, and so do you.
A night on the long scanners with her. By morning she has their burn marks on the screen.

events.title: Teo's list
events.text: Teo reads names off a folded paper at supper, slowly, every one. The men who broke Pier Nine.

outcomes.text: He folds the list back up. 'They hire out to the claims now,' he says. 'One of them's close.'
'A word with them,' he says. 'Just a word.' He doesn't eat the rest of his supper.

events.title: Survey stakes
events.text: Ama comes back from a walk with a Company survey stake in her hand. There's a line of them up the ridge. She knows whose.

outcomes.text: A day of pulling stakes. The wire is good, and the ridge is the colony's again.
'Harl,' she says. 'He signed my papers.' She leaves them standing, and goes to look for his tug.

events.title: Birthday card
events.text: A card for Dez on the supply drop: Old Halloran's birthday, the family all invited, collectors to see Dez home.

outcomes.text: Dez writes 'No' and signs it. You both know the collectors are coming anyway.
Dez tears it slowly. 'They'll come,' Dez says. 'Better we know where they'll be.'

events.title: Cold sleepers
events.text: A hulk with her cryo bay still powered: twelve pods, eleven dark, one with a pulse.

outcomes.text: Sleepers' rations, sealed for a long trip. They won't need them.
The bay's guns wake before the sleeper does.
Careful reading: the manifest says where the spares were stowed.
The squad closes the bay door softly on the way out.

events.title: Listing tanker
events.text: A tanker on her side, tanks half full, venting slowly from a crack in her hull.

outcomes.text: Fuel's as good as ore at the colony: it runs the forge.
The crack lets go while the squad's under it. A flash, a burn, and half the haul.
Good heavy hatches, unbolted and stacked in the hold.
She can vent the rest on her own.

events.title: Engine block
events.text: An engine torn loose from some ship, lying in the field like a fallen bell.

outcomes.text: A morning with the torch and a hold full of good metal.
It rolls when the last cut goes through. Someone was on the wrong side.
The engineer knows where the good parts sit and gets them out whole.
It's lain there this long.

events.title: Black box
events.text: In the wreckage, a black box still ticking, and a frame worth hauling.

outcomes.text: The pilot plays the last log: a ration drop she never reached, two kilometres north.
The frame comes away in three pieces and fits in the hold.
The frame comes away in three pieces. One of them on a foot.
It ticks on behind you as the ship lifts.

events.title: Ice pocket
events.text: A pocket of old ice under a ledge, clear as glass.

outcomes.text: Water enough for the colony's greens for a week.
The ledge comes down while the squad is under it.
Blocks for the coolers, stacked in the hold.
Too far from anything to bother with.

events.title: Claim marker
events.text: An old claim marker on the rock, its beacon dead, pointing at a seam nobody worked.

outcomes.text: Whoever set the marker knew rock. The seam is real, and somebody stashed spares by it.
The shaft they started was never shored. It isn't now.
A good post and a better battery.
Someone's claim. Let them keep it.

events.title: Grazers
events.text: A herd of something on the plain, slow and wide and grazing, paying the squad no mind.

outcomes.text: Meat for the colony, the first fresh in months.
It minds, after all. Someone gets trampled before it goes down.
The xenobiologist follows them all afternoon: what they graze on, the colony can grow.
They watch the ship lift without much interest.

events.title: Crashed lander
events.text: A lander nose-down in the dirt, her crew long gone, her bay doors open to the weather.

outcomes.text: Her bay had spares no weather got to.
Her frame shifts while the squad's inside. Plating, and a bruised crew.
Good plating, cut from the high side.
Someone may come back for her. Nobody has yet.
